purpose: Verify application-side 2x rendering without stretching a 1x capture or restarting the active Ubuntu desktop

mac.client: PaneFerryWindowHost release build, direct --app launch through the existing paired QUIC connection

ubuntu.session: independent Xvfb display, 4096x2160 pixels at 96 DPI

observed.display: Aspect-preserving presentation into 1470x815 Mac points; GTK toolbar and inserted text were visible at 2x source density
observed.input: Typed test text through the Mac host, then selected and deleted it; the editor title returned to an empty new document
observed.cleanup: Closed the test Mac host and stopped only the test editor and its private Xvfb; the original ChatGPT and Agent processes remained alive

launcher_trial.selected_setting: 200% (the user's existing saved preference was preserved)
launcher_trial.action: Clicked Text Editor in the rebuilt launcher's installed-app catalog
launcher_trial.result: A new named Mac WindowHost and independent Ubuntu Text Editor session opened over the existing paired QUIC connection; the Mac window received 2940x1630 H.264 pixels into 1470x815 points
launcher_trial.existing_sessions: The pre-existing Mac ChatGPT and Cockpit Tools hosts, Mac Node and network service, Ubuntu Agent, and original Ubuntu ChatGPT process remained running and connected; original ChatGPT still received its 1470x809 1x source

separate_chatgpt_probe.profile: temporary isolated HOME and profile; original account/profile untouched

limits: Existing running applications keep their original scale until they are restarted; the live ChatGPT session was not changed.
This short trial does not establish sustained frame rate or latency under load.
Wayland desktop windows already running at 1x were not migrated to a different output.
